neighbours.label: the opening quotation mark or dash that starts direct speech after a finished narrative sentence (vs the same speech reported indirectly)
fire: The captain looked out over the harbor for a long time. "We sail at dawn," he finally said.
Prices rose again last month, notes the economist. “Consumers are feeling it,” she said.

Анна долго смотрела в окно.
— Ты опять опоздал, — сказала она.
The vaccine was tested on thousands of volunteers. "The results are very encouraging," said Dr. Patel.

He closed the book and sighed.
— I think we should go home now.
Sales of electric cars doubled this year, the company reported. “Demand keeps growing,” its chief said.

Мальчик поднял голову и посмотрел на отца.
— А когда мы поедем на море?
The storm knocked out power across the valley. "We have never seen anything like it," one resident said.
quiet: The captain looked out over the harbor for a long time and finally said they would sail at dawn.
Prices rose again last month, notes the economist, who said consumers are feeling it.
Анна долго смотрела в окно и сказала, что он опять опоздал.
The vaccine was tested on thousands of volunteers, and Dr. Patel called the results very encouraging.
He closed the book, sighed, and suggested that they go home now.
Sales of electric cars doubled this year, the company reported, as demand keeps growing.
Мальчик поднял голову и спросил отца, когда они поедут на море.
The storm knocked out power across the valley, and residents said they had never seen anything like it.

notes: Probe: opening ' "' after a sentence 0.504, ' “' 0.554, Russian dialogue dash after narration 0.271/0.484; same content without a quote 0.017, en-dash in a page range 0.016. The Kamijou control without a dash still reached 0.171 at the final '.', so the sentence end before speech carries some activation. Near misses report the same speech indirectly in one sentence.
